def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (T : ℕ) (N : S1 Bool Bool), N.D9 → S1.D5 T N d15 → T ≤ N.d13

then T is less than or equal to the number of elements (cardinality) of N.A1.

translation:
Target defines the following proposition (without asserting or proving it): For every natural number T and every system N of type S1 Bool Bool—consisting of a finite type of nodes N.A1, a family of arbitrary state types N.A3 n for each n in N.A1, an initial global state N.a4 : (n : N.A1) → N.A3 n, a per-node update function N.a5 : (n : N.A1) → ((m : N.A1) → N.A3 m) → Bool → N.A3 n, and a readout function N.a6 : ((m : N.A1) → N.A3 m) → Bool—if both of the following hypotheses hold:

1. Acyclicity of dependencies (N.D9): say there is a directed dependency edge from m to n (for m, n in N.A1) if there exist two global states σ, σ' : (k : N.A1) → N.A3 k and a boolean input x such that σ k = σ' k for all k ≠ m and N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x. Then for every n in N.A1, there is no non-empty directed path from n back to n (no chain n = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n with k ≥ 1 and a directed edge from each c_i to c_{i+1}; this forbids both self-loops and longer cycles).

2. Agreement with d15 on inputs of length at most T (S1.D5 T N d15): for every finite sequence xs of booleans with xs.length ≤ T (including the empty sequence), running N on xs yields the same boolean output as running the specific system d15 on xs. Here, running a system on xs starts from its initial global state a4, updates the global state left to right for each input x in xs by sending σ to (fun n => a5 n σ x), and finally applies a6. The system d15 has a single node (Unit) with boolean state initialized to false, update rule σ () || x, and readout σ (); thus on any boolean sequence xs, d15 outputs false on the empty sequence and in general outputs true if and only if at least one element of xs is true (the left-fold of boolean OR starting from false).

then T is less than or equal to the number of elements (cardinality) of N.A1.

No requirements are placed on the per-node state types N.A3 n (they need not be finite or Bool), N.A1 is not required to be nonempty, the update and readout functions are arbitrary, and N is not required to agree with d15 on input sequences of length strictly greater than T.

divergences.description: Original lower bound specialized to a single 1-unit witness: P-D54 only makes an informal, qualified general claim that feedforward networks 'require many more neurons' (noting exceptions such as CNNs for image recognition), and P-H10 describes only the size of the unrolling-through-time construction ('copying the network 100 times' for 100 timesteps). Target strengthens this into a universal lower bound over all functionally equivalent acyclic systems, while narrowing the benchmark recurrent system to one fixed 1-unit Boolean OR-latch (d15) rather than an arbitrary k-unit recurrent network (for which unrolling yields T * k units). This matches the author's explicit acknowledgment that Target is their own lower bound for the one-unit example.

Abstract synchronous 1-step-delay model (S1) vs. neural networks: S1 replaces biological or artificial neurons with arbitrary finite collections of units having unrestricted (even infinite) state types A3 n and arbitrary update/readout functions a5, a6, which strengthens the lower bound. At the same time, S1 idealizes temporal processing as discrete synchronous ticks receiving one Boolean input per step with uniform 1-timestep delays per edge, excluding multi-step conduction delays or static spatial presentation of all T inputs at once (for which a single OR-neuron would suffice).

Feedforwardness via global functional dependence (N.D9): acyclicity is defined on the functional dependency graph N.D8 quantified over all global states in N.D1 (including unreachable ones), rather than structural/anatomical wiring or dependencies on reachable states alone. Structurally acyclic networks satisfy N.D9, and systems with globally inactive feedback loops are also covered, but systems with cycles active only on unreachable states are excluded.

Equivalence over all prefix lengths <= T (S1.D5): Target assumes agreement with d15 on every input sequence of length at most T (including the empty sequence), which is slightly stronger as a hypothesis than requiring agreement only on sequences of length T (though the lower bound T <= N.d13 would already hold from length-T agreement alone for T >= 1).

judgement.summary: Target accurately and soundly formalizes the author's stated lower bound—that any acyclic streaming system matching the 1-unit Boolean latch d15 over T steps requires at least T units—and appropriately supports the size-blowup point in P-D54 and P-H10. The divergences are minor, reflecting the author's acknowledged move from the sources' informal/construction-based remarks to a specific formal lower bound and standard discrete-time dynamical-system idealizations.
